questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Panama?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Panama on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Panama article.

questions.proof: Countries bordering Panama are Costa Rica in the Northwest and Colombia in the Southeast.

questions.prompt: True or false: “Panama shares a land border with Latvia.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look at the Atlas and see which countries touch it.

questions.proof: Panama borders Colombia, Costa Rica, United States.

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of Panama is Panama City.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Panama article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of Panama is Panama City.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Panama?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Demographics” part of the Panama article.

questions.proof: 8.6%: White European (Spanish-Canarian 74%, German 13%, Italian and Others 13%).

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Panama about 74,177 square kilometres; Belize about 22,966 square kilometres; Samoa about 2,842 square kilometres; Saint Vincent and the Grenadines about 389 square kilometres.
